idhma
(‘that which is lighted’)
------------------------------------------
In वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस् sticks of wood, of certain trees and plants, are used as fuel. They are called ‘idhma’. Usually the palāśa (Butea frondosa) and the khadira (Acacia cateclu) wood is used. The number of sticks used is 21, out of which 15 are put into the fire with the Sāmidhenī verses (eleven verses from the Ṛgveda recited by the hotā priest; for e.g., Ṛgveda 3.27.1, 6.16.10-12 and so on) which are normally chanted while kindling the fire. The other sticks are used for lining the border and for other purposes.

Idhmavāha
(‘one who carries sacrificial faggots’)
------------------------------------------
The sage Dṛḍhasyu or Dṛḍhāsya, the son of अगस्त्य and लोपामुद्रा, was physically so strong that he could transport sacrificial faggots normally carried by a thousand persons! Hence, he got this title from his ड़थेर्.
He was an expert in the Vedic lore and also very austere in his personal life. He was adopted as a son by another great sage Kratu.
